messages:
alex: Kicking off a canary for release v1.22.0 to eu-canary (30m window). deploy-bot is live. Watch /generate. Acceptance: p50 < 120ms, error-rate < 0.5%. Backout plan/checklist below, please ack.
deploy-bot: [deploy triggered] release=v1.22.0 target=eu-canary step=canary-5pct owner=@alex runbook=https://runbooks.redwood.com/canary-v1.22.0
jamal: Quick Q — what exactly do we do if latency spikes at the 10m mark? who toggles routing? :thinking_face:
maria: Short version: follow the canary escape-hatch runbook. TL;DR: 1) stop ramp, 2) pin traffic to previous model, 3) scale down new pool, 4) flush KV cache, 5) (if model-related regressions) revert DB toggle. Full runbook here: https://runbooks.redwood.com/escape-hatch-canary-v2
jamal: Can you paste the exact commands for pinning/routing? saves me hunting the console under pressure.
maria: Sure — commands we use via ops CLI:
```
# pin previous model for the /generate route
rwctl routing set --route /generate --model redwood/gptx-3.5-prod@sha1234
# unassign canary pool
rwctl capacity scale --pool eu-canary-v1 --replicas 0
# flush in-memory KV cache for prefix-based caching
rwctl cache flush --scope prefix --prefix "/generate"
```
Also you can use the Console quick action: Routes -> /generate -> Pin -> pick sha1234. If DB feature toggle is enabled use the feature flag dashboard to flip `model_v1_fallback=false`.
olivia: Adding: always leave a fallback model pinned for 10m after rollback; if rollback happens during a low-change window we still keep metrics retained for 1h. I will watch token latency and cost breakdown once pinned. :eyes:
sre-oncall: If we abort: I will own traffic pin + pool scale. Maria please own cache flush and Olivia take the post-rollback smoke test (3 calls, deterministic prompts). Jamal please start the rollback comms thread for customers if we end up cutting.
alex: Ack. Handed to oncall for traffic changes. jamal start comms if we flip. I will keep the deploy-bot announce pinned in this thread.
deploy-bot: [metric update] window=5m p50=95ms p95=210ms errors=0.12% route=/generate
alex: Canary looks green at 10m (p50=95ms, errors=0.12%). Proceeding to 50% ramp in 5m. If any of these thresholds breach (p50>120ms or errors>0.5%) — we hit the escape hatch immediately.
jamal: Noted. Quick checklist for backout (shortform):
- stop ramp
- `rwctl routing set --route /generate --model redwood/gptx-3.5-prod@sha1234`
- `rwctl capacity scale --pool eu-canary-v1 --replicas 0`
- `rwctl cache flush --scope prefix --prefix "/generate"`
- run smoke tests (olivia)
- update release notes + customer comms (jamal)
maria: Also: if latency spike is due to KV cache warming, consider a temporary ramp back to 10% and force background pre-warm with `rwctl cache prewarm --prefix "/generate" --model redwood/gptx-3.5-prod@sha1234` before full rollback. That often avoids DB toggles.
sre-oncall: Runbook link again for oncall: https://runbooks.redwood.com/escape-hatch-canary-v2 — contains rollforward vs rollback decision trees and exact command snippets. I put a quick TL;DR pinned message in the ops dashboard.
olivia: ACK and standing by. I'll post smoke test results here if we need a rollback. :thumbsup:
alex: Thanks team. continuing ramp. leaving archival notes in the release ticket after 50% completes.
